School
Valley Road
Green shoots have appeared in the soil by the pump station. At last, we can cultivate a few plots of clean land.
Seeds have been sown in the test plots. Farmers can now be assigned; each plot can be tended by up to four people.
Selected old parts can be melted down and reforged into standardized hand tools.
The workbench is ready. Toolmakers expend wood and scrap to craft useful tools.
Good tools make it possible to saw long beams. Several families can live under one longhouse roof.
Eight beds have been added to the longhouse. Before inviting more people to move in, we should weigh that against the food in the pot.
An old medical manual still holds instructions for cleaning and disinfecting wounds, and brewing basic medicines.
The clinic is open. Medical staff prepare basic medicines here, and routine care also expends medicinal herbs.
To pass on what we know, the memories in your head and the old craftsman's won't be enough.
Desks and chairs are in place at the school. Teachers expend wood and paper to turn scattered learning into knowledge that can be taught.
The valley's location is confirmed. For now, we can build a road connecting the pump station to the valley.
The road to the valley is now paved. The convoy delivers tools and medicine, and returns with a dependable supply of food.
Soil Identification
Several patches of toxin-cleared soil have been found around the pump station. Tender roots have finally taken hold in the gray earth.
Standard Hand Tools
The first batch of standardized axes and hoes passed testing. When tools break, we won't have to scour the hills for one-of-a-kind parts anymore.
Irrigation
Canals have brought fresh water from the pump station. As long as supplies keep reaching the outpost, the fields will yield more.
Food Preservation
Dry rations can now be portioned and sealed. Less food is lost on the road, and distant settlements no longer feel out of reach.
Public Records
Scrap paper collected from the transit station has been bound into books. Debts and hard-won skills now have a written record.
Public Health
Drinking water and waste now flow through separate channels. The clinic can protect more neighbors' lives.
Basic Education
A rare old textbook has been hand-copied many times. At last, the settlement can train its own teachers.
Road Maintenance
The supply crew has marked broken bridges and gentle slopes along the route. We can now follow the traders' tracks to seek out settlements in the valley.

The ore vein's course has been mapped. We must shore up the shaft and lay minecart tracks before anyone can go underground.
The mine shaft is shored up. Miners expend tools to steadily extract iron ore from the mapped vein.
An old mine map marks an exposed coal seam. Mining it will also require tools and ventilation shafts.
The coal mine has been ventilated. Coal miners can supply coal for fires and the power plant we plan to build.
The workshop furnace can finally melt ore. It's time to build a dedicated smelting furnace.
The smelting furnace is fired up. Smelters turn iron ore and coal into iron ingots, while black smoke gathers under the roof.
Iron ingots can be machined into meshing gears and drive shafts. The machine shop needs workers who can read and understand blueprints.
The machine shop is up and running. Without electricity, parts can only be filed by hand, slowly; with power, the same iron yields more precise work.
The small generator has passed its test run. The power plant needs coal, spare parts, and an electrician on constant watch.
Power cables now reach the work area. Electricians stoke the furnace and maintain the equipment day and night; if the generator stops, the lathe stops too.
Coal smoke settles on the rooftops and fills people's lungs. Water curtains and filters can trap the soot.
The smoke treatment facility is connected to the exhaust pipe. With a steady supply of power, wood, and spare parts, the air over the work area can be cleaner.
Shallow Mining
The support and ventilation methods have been tested. We no longer have to rely on scraps from the prewar ruins for iron.
